ov: Medium-sized rodents, the best known being the brown and black rats that live alongside people. The brown rat has been bred into the pet “fancy rat” and the laboratory rat.

why.et: Rat meat is taboo in some cultures but a dietary staple in others.

len: About 40 cm including the tail (brown rat)
rg: Every region inhabited by people except Antarctica. There are 56 known species, many found only on islands.
df: A true omnivore that eats almost anything, though cereals form much of a brown rat’s diet.

cf.tip: Mice and rats are told apart mainly by size: “rat” is used for the bigger kinds, “mouse” for the smaller.

notes: The existing fact (laughs when tickled) is confirmed: the Brown rat article describes ultrasonic "chirping" likened to laughter.
